tokens.name: paper
tokens.usage: Page ground. Paper is the cool mineral off-white of a clean hall, and Hall is the data hall with the lights down. Never pure white.

tokens.name: paper-raised
tokens.usage: Raised surfaces: evidence slips, menus, form fields.

tokens.name: rule
tokens.usage: Hairlines and dividers. Decorative only, never the sole boundary of a control.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and solid buttons, on paper and paper-raised. 15.3:1 on paper.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary text, captions and mono labels, on paper and paper-raised. 6.6:1 on paper and 7.1:1 on hall.

tokens.name: hall
tokens.usage: Fixed deep ground for moments that stay dark in both themes: the reticle label, the phone dock screen, the dark hall chapter.

tokens.name: link
tokens.usage: Verified. This is the port-LED green, used for light: LEDs, glows, outlines, laser sheets, dots. Never as text on paper (1.6:1). As a fill, put hall text on it.

tokens.name: link-ink
tokens.usage: Verified as text or icon on paper and paper-raised (5.2:1), and on the hall theme's grounds. Also the hover fill of solid buttons.

tokens.name: drift
tokens.usage: Mismatch between records and reality. It's the amber glow on a drifting unit, the only warm colour in the system. Light only; never text on paper.

tokens.name: drift-ink
tokens.usage: Mismatch as text or an icon, on paper (5.1:1) and on hall (9.0:1). Pair it with a ▲ glyph or a word so it's never colour alone.

tokens.name: record
tokens.usage: What the paperwork says: the CMDB ghost, dashed wireframes, record swatches. Lines and fills only (2.7:1 on paper).

tokens.name: record-ink
tokens.usage: Record-related text such as 'Recorded · CMDB' labels, on paper (6.2:1) and hall (8.7:1).

tokens.name: aluminium
tokens.usage: The hero cabinet's anodised shell. It's the one light object in a dark scene, so keep it in both themes.

tokens.name: chassis
tokens.usage: Equipment faces and device bodies in 3D and illustration.

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: 2px keyboard focus ring with a 3px offset.

tokens.name: chart-track
tokens.usage: Empty track behind progress and category bars, and zero cells in heatmaps.

tokens.name: chart-grid
tokens.usage: Chart gridlines. Keep them recessive.

tokens.name: chart-used
tokens.usage: Occupied rack units in capacity strips.

tokens.name: chart-free
tokens.usage: Free units and free ports: the neutral part of a part-to-whole.

tokens.name: heat-1
tokens.usage: Mismatch heatmap, 1–2. Single-hue amber ramp, light to dark.

tokens.name: heat-2
tokens.usage: Mismatch heatmap, 3–5.

tokens.name: heat-3
tokens.usage: Mismatch heatmap, 6–9.

tokens.name: heat-4
tokens.usage: Mismatch heatmap, 10 and above.

styles.name: display-hero
styles.sample: Know what's really in the rack.
styles.usage: Hero headline, once per page. Scale with clamp(2.5rem, 5.2vw, 4.5rem) (hamina text-5xl -> text-7xl). No ch-cap: it takes the reading column's width and balances.

styles.name: display-chapter
styles.usage: Chapter headlines. clamp(1.875rem, 3vw, 2.25rem) (hamina text-3xl -> sm:text-4xl). One plain sentence; never split into bold and light halves.

styles.name: figure
styles.usage: Big numbers such as the agreement meter. Same step as a chapter headline, so a figure and a headline sit on one scale.

styles.name: lede
styles.sample: One phone sweep reads every device, port and cable.
styles.usage: The single sentence under each headline, in ink-muted (hamina text-lg + leading-relaxed). Width comes from the reading column, not a max-width of its own.

styles.name: ui
styles.usage: Buttons at 600 and nav links at 500, both 14px (text-sm). Sentence case, never uppercase.

styles.name: readout
styles.usage: Anything a machine would print: rack units, device IDs, port counts, timestamps. Reticle, 3D tags, phone HUD.

styles.name: record
styles.usage: Evidence slips and other machine records (mono at the text-xs step).

styles.name: figure-mono
styles.usage: Axis labels and legends inside the analytics cards.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Icon to label.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Tag padding and small gaps.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Button groups and list item padding.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Evidence-slip padding and the minimum phone gutter.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Headline to its sentence.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Between a headline block and what follows it.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Nav items; lede to the buttons under it.

tokens.name: space-10
tokens.usage: Between blocks inside a chapter.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Large page gutter.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: Nav height to the first headline.

tokens.name: space-20
tokens.usage: Between major bands.

tokens.name: space-24
tokens.usage: Footer top padding (hamina py-24).

tokens.name: shell
tokens.usage: Max content width, centred. Every band pads to it, so the page has one left edge. Matches hamina's max-w-7xl.

tokens.name: gutter
tokens.usage: Page gutter at small widths; --bleed grows past it to keep --shell centred.

tokens.name: nav-h
tokens.usage: Fixed nav height. Sticky copy and the stage box both start below it.

tokens.name: copy-w
tokens.usage: The reading column. Viewport-tracking so the 3D stage keeps the same share of the screen at every width.

tokens.name: stage-h
tokens.usage: The band the 3D stage gets when the layout stacks (under 900px). The script reads it to frame the rack.

tokens.name: chapter
tokens.usage: Minimum scroll length of a chapter.

tokens.name: radius-none
tokens.usage: Rules and meters.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Tags, slip tags and the reticle label. Hardware is square-cornered, and so is the UI.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Buttons and cards. This is the largest radius on any UI element.

tokens.name: radius-device
tokens.usage: Only the phone dock frame. It's the one rounded object, so it reads as a device, not as UI.

tokens.name: shadow-slip
tokens.usage: Evidence slips and the phone dock: an object resting on the page. Nothing else casts a shadow.
